full_judgment:
10. Learned Advocate for the appellants submits that occurrence as per first information report took place at 4-00 PM on 28-9-89 but first information report was lodged at 12 hours on 29-9-89 and above delay was not properly explained by prosecution although thana was only 12 miles off from the place of occurrence and village of the informant. According to him, such unexplained inordinate delay will bring adverse presumption against prosecution. 

 12. Learned Advocate shows from record that prosecution examined 8 PWs out of 17 CS witnesses. PW 4, 5 constables Jahurul Islam and A Kashem, PW 6 Magistrate Anil Kumar Chakraborty, PW 7 investigation officer SI Idris Ali and PW 8 Dr. Mozibur Rahman (submitting post-mortem report after post-mortem examination) were formal and official witnesses. Out of them PW 5 was tendered. PWs 1-3 were public witnesses including informant. Muslim (PW 1) PW 2 and 3 Shahidullah and Mukthar Hossain were declared/hostile and cross examined by prosecution alone as they did not support prosecution story. Sole and only evidence was of PW 1 informant Muslim. He contended that reliance on the sole evidence of PW 1 alone without any other corroboration will be unsafe and risky to have decision against the convict-appellant, particularly when first information report by PW 1 and evidence of PW 1 at the trial were found to be, not in conformity with each other, on some material facts, He refers to first information report. Exhibit 1 and shows that in first information report PW 1 informant disclosed that he saw the accused coming out of a ditch on the bank of the tank and saw them running away through muddy watery land to west of tank, PW 1 stated in deposition at the trial that he saw the accused leaving by the west bank of the tank. PW 1 disclosed in cross examination that he saw the accused from northern bank of the tank and recognised them from back side from distance of 400 cubits. PW 1 also disclosed that there were bushes and bamboo grove on the western bank of the tank. Learned Advocate showing above anomaly and discrepant facts contends that the story of recognition by PW 1 cannot be trustworthy at all. He shows that prosecution withheld CS witnesses Nos. 2, 3, 5, 7-11 and 16 without any reasonable explanation and it will give rise to adverse presumption under section 114(g) Evidence Act. 

 13. Learned Advocate contends that abconsion sometimes takes place due to apprehension of police torture and harassment and absconsion cannot itself be a ground to have adverse presumption against the accused. He contends that appellant Suruj Miah was absconding during trial of the case, but after judgment he surrendered to Court below wherefrom he was sent to custody. He contends that absconsion of Suruj Miah cannot be considered as a positive ground against him. 

 19. Learned Advocate refers to the first information report Exhibit I wherein informant PW 1 stated that he found his son Shamim groaning in muddy earth in the ditch. Nothing stated in first information report Exhibit 1 or in deposition of PW 1 at the trial about wearing apparel (cloth) of victim Shamim. He contends that the wearing apparels of the victim were likely to have blood stained marks during occurrence. But said wearing apparels of the victim were not produced at the trial to be marked Mat. Exhibit although from column No. 5 of the charge-sheet he shows that there was mention about an old half pant as alamat. He argues that said old half pant was not produced at the trial to show whether there was any blood stain or muddy earth mark on the same to corroborate the above first information report story. Above anomaly will affect the manner of occurrence and will give rise to adverse presumption against prosecution. 

 30. Both informant Moslem Miah and 3 accused namely, Zakir, Suruj Miah and Sadek Ali were men of same village Shilondia as evidence from Column No. 2 of first information report Exhibit 1 and also from CS filed after investigation by police. From first information report (Exhibit 1) it appears further that Matlab thana was 12 miles off from the place of occurrence village namely, Shalindia. In Exhibit 1 (first information report) and in deposition at the trial PW 1 informant clearly stated that after seeing the dead body of his son Shamim he (informant) became senseless. After occurrence at 4-00 PM on 28-9-89 and after regaining sense the informant Moslem could not go to Matlab PS at night following 28-9-89. He went on 29-9-89 and lodged first information report at 12 hours in Matlab PS covering above distance of 12 miles from their village Shindia. In above view the delay as occasioned in lodging first information report at 12 hours on 29-9-89 cannot be inordinate one to give rise to any adverse presumption against prosecution as alleged. 

 32. An argument was offered on behalf of defence (appellant) that there has been difference and anomaly in material particulars between averments in first information report Exhibit 1 and those in the deposition at the trial of PW 1 and said anomaly would create adverse presumption against the truth of above facts stated by informant PW 1 and also would create benefit of doubt.
